## Cumulative frequency polygon · an ogive {#l2-ogive-definition .compact}

A **cumulative frequency polygon** is also called an **ogive**.

::: {.split .ogive-intro-layout}
::: {.column-block}
```{=html}
<div data-module="ogive-intro"></div>
```
:::
::: {.column-block}

- Mark the **top-right corner of each cumulative histogram bar**: its upper class boundary and cumulative frequency.
- Start at **zero cumulative frequency**, at the first lower boundary.
- Join neighbouring points with **straight line segments**.
- The final height is the **total number of observations**.

:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
An ogive displays the running total. A horizontal guide at half the total helps estimate the median.
:::

::: notes
The pale bars show the cumulative frequency histogram. The ogive passes through each bar's top-right corner, preceded by the zero point at the first lower boundary. Leave a half-column gap between the vertical axis and the first bar, matching CambridgeMATHS NSW Stage 6 Mathematics Extension 1 Year 11 (second edition), p. 615. The zero point stays at the first bar’s lower boundary, not at the vertical axis. The horizontal scale and all class boundaries remain unchanged.

The illustrative integer scores 1,2,3,4 have frequencies 2,5,4,1. Their unit-width bins have boundaries 0.5–4.5, giving ogive points (0.5,0),(1.5,2),(2.5,7),(3.5,11),(4.5,12). In particular cf=7 at boundary 2.5 means seven observations have integer scores at most 2. For continuous classes a≤x<b, the count at b is below b. Join with straight segments, not a smoothed curve. Example 3.9 will distinguish the ogive estimate from the exact discrete median obtained from ordered positions.
:::
